subject.title: fix(update): dev channel update builds from an unverified checkout at the git install path

question: Should package-to-dev conversion permanently refuse every pre-existing `OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR` path, reclaiming only a checkout proven by matching updater-owned shared-state and in-checkout markers?
rationale: This intentionally changes an existing update workflow and imposes a one-time operator action; code review cannot decide the acceptable upgrade and support trade-off without owner intent.

options.title: Approve fail-closed conversion policy
options.body: Keep the PR’s rule that only an unused destination or a verifiably updater-owned interrupted checkout can be used, preventing adoption of attacker-controlled Git state.

options.title: Require a compatibility migration
options.body: Define a narrowly safe, documented migration path for existing destinations before accepting any conversion behavior that reuses them.

options.title: Defer the policy change
options.body: Pause this PR until the updater owner chooses a permanent conversion contract and support posture.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed conversion policy
recommendation.body: Keep the PR’s rule that only an unused destination or a verifiably updater-owned interrupted checkout can be used, preventing adoption of attacker-controlled Git state.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR discussion explicitly requests this person’s approval on the precise updater policy at issue.
